title: Architecture and UML models
subtitle: Draw the system before you build it: boxes for structure, sequences for behaviour.

arch.title: Architectural styles
arch.body: Architecture = the major components and how they communicate. Common styles: layered (UI → business → data), client–server, MVC, pipe-and-filter, microservices, event-driven. Each trades simplicity, scalability and independence.

mvc.title: MVC request path
mvc.body: Model holds data and rules, View renders, Controller handles input and coordinates. Changing the UI does not touch the rules.

uc.title: Use case diagrams
uc.body: Actors (people or systems) sit outside a system boundary; ovals are use cases; lines show participation; include (mandatory sub-behaviour) and extend (optional) relate use cases.

class.title: Class diagrams
class.body: Boxes with name, attributes, operations; lines show association (with multiplicity), aggregation/composition (whole–part), inheritance (is-a).

seq.title: Sequence diagrams
seq.body: Lifelines run downward; arrows are messages in order; dashed arrows are returns. They show one scenario of one use case.

dfd.title: Data flow and activity diagrams
dfd.body: A DFD shows processes (circles), stores (open rectangles), external entities (squares) and data flows; it has levels — level 0 is the context diagram. An activity diagram shows the control flow of a process with decisions and parallel forks.
dfd.steps: A DFD process has 3 inputs and 1 output: it must change data, not just pass it on — otherwise it is not a process.
